questions.questionText: The magnetic force acting on a charge q moving with velocity v in a magnetic field B is given by:
questions.explanation: The magnetic Lorentz force on a moving charge is defined as the cross product of velocity and magnetic field, given by F = q(v × B).

questions.questionText: The SI unit of magnetic field strength B is:
questions.explanation: The SI unit of magnetic field strength B is Tesla (T), where 1 T = 1 N s C⁻¹ m⁻¹.

questions.questionText: A charged particle moves parallel to a uniform magnetic field. The path followed by the particle is:
questions.explanation: When velocity is parallel to the magnetic field, θ = 0°, so the magnetic force F = qvB sin(0°) = 0. The particle continues in a straight line.

questions.questionText: According to the Biot-Savart law, the magnetic field dB due to a current element I dl at a distance r varies as:
questions.explanation: Biot-Savart law states that dB = (μ₀/4π) (I dl sin θ / r²), showing an inverse-square dependence on distance r.

questions.questionText: The magnetic field inside an ideal, infinitely long current-carrying solenoid is:

options.text: Inversely proportional to distance from axis

questions.explanation: Inside an ideal long solenoid, the magnetic field is uniform, parallel to the axis, and given by B = μ₀ n I.

questions.questionText: Two parallel conductors carrying currents in the same direction will:

options.text: Exert no force on each other

questions.explanation: Parallel currents carrying charges in the same direction produce magnetic fields that result in an attractive force between the wires.

questions.questionText: The magnetic dipole moment m of a planar loop carrying current I and enclosing area A is:
questions.explanation: The magnetic dipole moment of a current loop is defined as the product of current and loop area, vectorially m = I A.

questions.questionText: To convert a moving coil galvanometer into an ammeter, one must connect:
questions.explanation: A galvanometer is converted into an ammeter by connecting a low resistance called shunt in parallel with its coil.

questions.questionText: An electron enters a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T with a velocity of 3 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ perpendicular to the field. The magnetic force on the electron is:
A proton moves in a circular path of radius 0.2 m in a magnetic field of 0.5 T perpendicular to its motion. The kinetic energy of the proton is closest to:
questions.explanation: Radius r = q v B / m gives v = q B r / m. K = (1/2) m v² = q² B² r² / (2 m) = (1.6×10⁻¹⁹)² × 0.5² × 0.2² / (2 × 1.67×10⁻²⁷) ≈ 7.66×10⁻¹⁴ J ≈ 0.48 MeV.

questions.questionText: The magnetic field at the center of a circular current loop of radius R carrying current I is B. The magnetic field on the axis at a distance R from the center is:
questions.explanation: B_center = μ₀ I / 2R. On axis at x = R, B_axis = μ₀ I R² / [2(R² + R²)³ᐟ²] = μ₀ I / (4√2 R) = B_center / 2√2.

questions.questionText: A long straight wire carries a current of 35 A. The magnitude of the magnetic field at a point 20 cm from the wire is:
A solenoid of length 0.5 m has 500 turns and carries a current of 2 A. The magnetic field near the center inside the solenoid is:
Two parallel long wires separated by 5 cm in air carry currents of 10 A and 20 A in opposite directions. The force per unit length between them is:
questions.explanation: F/L = (μ₀ I₁ I₂) / (2π d) = (4π × 10⁻⁷ × 10 × 20) / (2π × 0.05) = 8 × 10⁻⁴ N m⁻¹. Opposite currents repel.

questions.questionText: A square loop of side 10 cm carrying a current of 2 A is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T making an angle of 30° with the normal to the loop. The torque experienced by the loop is:
questions.explanation: Magnetic moment m = I A = 2 × (0.1)² = 0.02 A m². Torque τ = m B sin θ = 0.02 × 0.5 × sin 30° = 0.005 = 2.5 × 10⁻³ N m.

questions.questionText: A galvanometer has a resistance of 50 Ω and gives full scale deflection for a current of 2 mA. The shunt resistance required to convert it into an ammeter of range 0 to 5 A is:

A charged particle carrying charge q enters a region with uniform electric field E = E ĵ and uniform magnetic field B = B k̂. The particle passes undeflected through the region. The velocity vector of the particle must be:
questions.explanation: For zero net force, qE + q(v × B) = 0, so E = -(v × B). Given E = E ĵ and B = B k̂, setting v = v î gives v × B = v B (î × k̂) = -v B ĵ. Thus qE ĵ - q v B ĵ = 0, which yields v = E/B in the +î direction.

questions.questionText: A wire carrying current I is bent into the shape of a regular hexagon of side length a. The magnitude of the magnetic field at the center of the hexagon is:
questions.explanation: Distance from center to each side is d = a cos 30° = a √3 / 2. Field from one side is B1 = (μ₀ I / 4π d) (sin 30° + sin 30°) = μ₀ I / (2π a √3). Total B = 6 B1 = 6 μ₀ I / (2π a √3) = (√3 μ₀ I) / (π a).

questions.questionText: A non-conducting circular ring of radius R has a total charge Q uniformly distributed over its circumference. If the ring rotates about its central axis with constant angular speed ω, the magnetic field at its center is:
questions.explanation: Equivalent current generated by rotating ring is I = Q / T = Q ω / (2π). The magnetic field at the center of a circular current loop is B = μ₀ I / (2 R) = μ₀ (Q ω / 2π) / (2 R) = (μ₀ Q ω) / (4π R).

questions.questionText: A galvanometer coil of resistance 100 Ω gives full scale deflection for 1 mA. To convert it into a voltmeter reading up to 10 V, the series resistance required is R1. To convert it into an ammeter reading up to 1 A, the shunt resistance required is R2. The ratio R1 / R2 is closest to:
